To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nine mAbs were produced that reacted with synthetic T-HSA, three of which did not react with desialyted T-HSA, but did react with natural sources of T antigen.

(1) mAbs reactive with synthetic T-HSA were produced after immunization with T-KLH, (2) mAb 145.2 reacted with both synthetic and natural sTn and natural Tn, (3) mAb B72.2 reacted with sTn and OSM, and (4) mAb CC49 reacted with OSM, but not sTn-HAS
the mAbs 3G5, 2G10, 3F11, 3G12, 3G8, and 145.22 are all useful for detecting Tn, T and sialylated (6-->2) Tn antigens, and that 3G5 and 145. 22 may be useful for detecting T antigen in human tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a panel of mAbs to T, sTn, and Tn antigens, and the characterization of their epitope specificities by ELISA and by immunohistochemistry.
the production and characterization of murine mAbs that recognize T, Tn and sTn antigens.
the development of mAbs to T, Tn and sTn, and the characterization of these mAbs by ELISA and tissue staining.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epitope specificities for mAbs 3H10, 3H11, 3H12, 3H13, 3H14, 3H15, 3H16, 3H17, 3H18, 3H19, 3H20, 3H21, 145.22, B72.3, and CC49 are distinct.
the epitope recognized by mAb CC49 has not been defined.
mAb 145. 22 is specific for sTn and mAb B72. 3 is specific for sialylated and desialyated T antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mAb 145.2 is a new mAb reactive with natural and synthetic Tn, and that mAbs B72.3 and CC49 react with sTn, T, sialyated (2-->3) T, and sialylated (3-->6) T.
the mAbs 1A7, 1A8, 2B1, 4A5, 6B3, 6B5, 6G7, 6H5, 6H7, 8A7, and 145.22 are reactive with synthetic and natural sources of T, sialyl-T, and Tn.
the mAbs produced by us react with a variety of Tn, Tn, T antigens, while B72.3 and CC49 react with a subset of Tn, sTn, and T antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for more specific mAbs to these antigens.
there are multiple monoclonal antibodies that recognize the T, Tn and sialylated-Tn antigens.
the epitope specificities of mAbs reactive with synthetic T, sTn and natural Tn are not identical.
